title: The Missing Discovery Layer in Global Payments  * link below in the comments  #GlobalPayments #PaymentTechnology #FinancialIT
summary:
Today, a merchant can accept a payment from a customer on another continent in a few seconds. Finding a provider willing to process those payments can take the same merchant several months.
We can settle a cross-border payment in seconds, tokenize a card across a dozen providers, and route every transaction to the acquirer most likely to approve it. Yet when a business asks the most basic question in this industry, which payment provider will actually work with us?, the answer is still assembled by hand. It comes from provider websites, warm introductions, private chats, and a spreadsheet someone started three markets ago.
After two decades of building payment infrastructure, I have come to see this as one of the most underrated problems in our industry. People do notice it. They have just learned to live with it.
What ‘fit’ means in payments
Consider a subscription software company registered in Estonia, with customers in Brazil and Germany. Its volumes are modest and growing. It needs cards, Pix, SEPA Direct Debit, and recurring billing that handles retries properly.
A provider page saying ‘we support Brazil' answers almost none of this company's questions. It needs to know:
Whether the provider accepts Estonian entities;
How it treats subscription businesses;
Whether wallets and cards can run through the same account;
Which currencies it settles in;
Whether a short processing history will count against it.
So when people ask me for the best payment provider, I usually have to ask several questions back before I can say anything useful. A provider with an excellent reputation may turn a merchant down within a day because the merchant falls outside its risk policy. The merchant then starts again with the next name on the list.
Provider websites describe products and coverage well. They rarely say which kinds of businesses the provider actually approves, on what terms, and in which markets. Yet that is the information merchants spend most of their time trying to find.
A bigger market with the same old search process
The growth of paytech has given merchants more options: regional specialists, alternative payment methods and new competitors to traditional acquiring banks. Merchants are prepared to use them. Capgemini's World Payments Report 2026 found that 40% of small and mid-sized merchants plan to move to paytech providers within a year. It also found that 69% expect fast and seamless onboarding.
Each new option, though, is another company to research and qualify, and the tools for that research were built for a smaller market:
Directories list companies.
Rankings reduce a complex decision to a single score.
Advice from another merchant can help, but it reflects their jurisdiction, industry, and volumes, which may have little in common with yours.
Merchants have no reliable way to see which providers might suit their particular case and why. They also cannot easily tell which requirements could cause trouble, or what they should confirm with a provider before applying.
The industry has spent years on data standards and interoperability so that payment systems can exchange information. Very little comparable effort has gone into describing the companies that run those systems in a consistent format.
What a better provider search looks like
We built PayAtlas to address this. The platform currently covers more than 1400 payment providers and related paytech companies across 214 countries, 285 payment methods, and 72 industries. A list that long would be of limited use on its own, so most of our work focuses on what you can do with the data. We organize the product in three parts.
Understanding the market. PayAtlas links each provider to the countries it serves, the services it offers, the payment methods it supports, and the industries it works with, along with regulators and other parts of the ecosystem. If you are planning to enter a new country, PayAtlas Insights shows how many providers operate there and which services tend to come with which payment methods. That way you can study the market before you contact anyone. If you run a paytech company, the same data shows where competition is dense and where it is thin.
Narrowing the choice. In PayAtlas Navigator, you enter your business type, geography, and payment requirements and receive a set of providers that may suit you. For each one, Navigator explains why it was included and which factors could affect your onboarding. You can then put two candidates into the provider comparison and review coverage, methods, and capabilities against the same criteria, without switching between websites and sales decks.
Reaching providers. With PayAtlas Connect, you describe your requirements once and share the request with relevant providers. Those that can support your business respond, and you compare their offers in one place instead of repeating the same introductory call with a dozen companies.
What changes for providers when requests are structured
Poor discovery costs providers time too. Their sales and compliance teams handle many inquiries from businesses they could never onboard because of geography, industry, volume, or risk. Some of those inquiries take days to qualify before the mismatch becomes clear.
Take a regional acquirer in Latin America that specializes in iGaming and travel. Through their website contact form, they may receive requests from a European fashion retailer, a US crypto exchange, and a newly launched marketplace with no transaction history. They cannot onboard any of them. Each request still takes someone's time: a reply, a call, or at least a check against the risk policy.
When the same acquirer receives a structured request, they can see upfront where the merchant is registered, what the merchant sells, which countries it targets, and what volumes it expects. Their team can then focus on requests that match their licenses and risk appetite.
When a request arrives through a structured process, providers already know the merchant's business model, target markets, required payment methods, and operational needs, so they can decide quickly whether to engage.
A map of the wider ecosystem
Matching merchants with providers is the first use of this data. Payments involve many connected parties, including providers, acquirers, banks, technology vendors, regulators, payment methods, currencies, industries, consultants and merchants.
Once those relationships are recorded in a structured form, the data can reveal:
Which markets have too few providers;
Where competition is growing;
Which industries struggle most to find payment partners;
Which capabilities are becoming standard.
The way businesses research suppliers is also shifting. More teams now start with a search engine or an AI assistant before they speak to anyone. These tools can only draw on information that is structured, current, and publicly available. Knowledge kept in private chats and sales presentations never reaches them, so answers miss providers and markets described only there.
Where this leaves the industry
Payments will stay diverse. Regulation differs by country, consumers prefer different methods, and providers specialize in particular industries and risk profiles. This variety lets specialized providers serve businesses that a global platform would overlook, and it is unlikely to disappear.
What can improve is how easily a merchant finds its way through that variety. With good data, a merchant should be able to:
Search the market;
Compare real options;
Understand the reasoning behind a recommendation;
Contact the right providers without relying on luck or personal connections.
We built PayAtlas for that purpose, because the choice of provider shapes every part of a payment setup that follows.

title: Creditspring and London South Bank Colleges Partner to Build Money Confidence for Young Adults
summary:
Creditspring, the subscription-based credit provider is on a mission to improve financial stability across the UK and has partnered with London South Bank Colleges to deliver Managing Money, a financial education programme designed to help young adults build the knowledge and confidence to manage their finances as they move into adulthood.
Through a series of student talks, the programme will cover the everyday financial decisions young people increasingly face as they begin earning. From understanding payslips, budgeting, credit, repayments and where to seek support when money feels difficult to manage.
The partnership responds to a clear gap in financial preparedness. With many young people about to take on greater independence, research from Creditspring suggests that essential borrowing terms and the consequences of missed payments are not always well understood.
Among 18-24-year-olds, fewer than half say they understand APR (45%) or what a minimum repayment means (46%). Just over half (52%) know that missing a loan repayment can damage their credit score, compared with 83% of people aged over 55. More than a third (35%) believe that 0% interest definitely means there are no additional costs.
The findings also point to a reluctance to ask for help early. Only one in five 18-24-year-olds (20%) say they would contact their lender if they were struggling with a repayment, compared with almost half (49%) of those aged over 55.
Financial pressure is not limited to bills and borrowing. The research also found that 91% of Gen Z respondents (14-29 years old) felt social plans put pressure on their finances. To manage those costs, 25% said they had taken on extra work or shifts, 18% had skipped meals and 22% had sold personal belongings.
Managing Money will give students a straightforward grounding in the choices and trade-offs behind these figures, helping them ask better questions, recognise potential costs and build habits that support their financial wellbeing over time.
The programme builds on Creditspring’s wider commitment to financial inclusion and education. Earlier this year, Creditspring’s People & Culture Partner, Linda Murphy-Ericsson, spoke with London South Bank Colleges students at an International Women’s Day event about her career journey, ambition, opportunity, and the value of support and allyship.
Neil Kadagathur, CEO and Founder of Creditspring, said: “Financial confidence should not be something people have to learn through costly mistakes. As young adults begin earning and making decisions independently, understanding the basics of credit, repayments and asking for help can make a real difference to their long-term financial stability.
“Creditspring’s mission is to improve financial stability across the UK. We believe subscription finance can offer a safer, simpler and more affordable way for people to access short-term liquidity when they need it, but access alone is not enough. People also need clear, practical education that helps them understand the decisions in front of them and stay safe as they build their financial future.”
Alicia Maker, Careers Lead at London South Bank Colleges said: “Preparing students for the world of work also means helping them prepare for the financial responsibilities that come with it. The Managing Money programme gives our students practical, accessible information at a point when it can have a lasting impact. We are delighted to work with Creditspring on a programme that puts confidence, informed choices and financial wellbeing first.”

content: Creditspring has partnered with London South Bank Colleges to launch the Managing Money financial education programme for young adults. The initiative aims to improve financial literacy, addressing gaps in understanding around credit, budgeting, and debt management among 18-to-24-year-olds. Through student talks, the programme equips young people with practical skills to navigate financial independence as they enter adulthood.

title: Two Months' Revenue, Unlocked Today: ANNA and YouLend Launch Embedded Finance for Small Businesses
summary:
ANNA, the UK business account that handles your admin so you don't have to, has partnered with embedded finance provider YouLend to bring this funding into the ANNA app.
Rather than applying for a loan and waiting weeks for a decision, the funding works as an advance on a business's own trading history. Businesses receive funding in as little as 24 hours, against their projected revenue, and it is settled automatically from a share of revenue as it continues to come in - adjusted to seasonality and slow days in your business.
The launch comes as small businesses report increasingly tight cash flow more broadly. Analysis from the Credit Protection Association found 42% of small firms were paid late in the past year - more than double the rate from summer 2024 - while appetite for traditional external funding has fallen to a record low of 40%, down from 63% in 2023. 
Businesses are using the funding to stock up before a busy season, cover payroll during a slower month, or fund the kind of investment that turns a good month into a better one. This could mean taking on new inventory ahead of anticipated high demand to paying rent on a new site or refurbishing an existing shop or restaurant.
The partnership also reflects demand ANNA was already seeing organically. As of today, over 1,531 ANNA customers have already signed up to use YouLend with a total funding volume of £44.8m. This equates to an average of £29,300 per business, as part of their working capital solutions. The existing appetite for merchant cash advance among ANNA's customers was a core driver behind the two companies partnering up to fully embed this financial product into the ANNA customer experience and enable businesses to get access to funds almost instantly. The partnership reinforces ANNA's strategy to connect customers with trusted, market-leading providers of essential business services, all in one place.
Boris Diakonov, Co-CEO of ANNA, said: "Most small businesses aren't short on revenue, they're short on timing. The money's coming, it's just not here yet. This isn't about waiting for a bank to say yes to a loan, with YouLend it's about putting the revenue your business is already generating to work now, today - instead of waiting for it to land sometime next week. We built ANNA to get admin out of people's way - waiting for your own money to arrive shouldn't be one more thing on that list."
"Partnering with ANNA means we can meet businesses where they already manage their finances, rather than asking them to go looking for funding elsewhere," said Dan Sinclair-Taylor, Country Head UK & ROI at YouLend. "ANNA customers already trust the app to handle their admin, so embedding funding into that same experience just made sense, it's one less relationship for a business to manage, not another one to set up."
Eligible ANNA customers are pre-qualified for funding based on their trading history and guided seamlessly through the application process within the app. Rather than relying solely on assets or credit history, funding amounts are calculated using revenue the business is already generating including income from marketplace sales and payment provider flows. YouLend, which provides the funding, claims 80% of pre-qualified customers go on to be approved (eligibility criteria apply).

Already, thousands of customers have utilized the service, reflecting strong demand for integrated financial tools.

title: Changing Lanes: Cross-Border Payment Providers in New Race to Win SME Loyalty
summary:
Nine in 10 (91%) small and medium-sized businesses (SMEs) trading internationally are set to switch their current cross-border payment provider in the next two years, according to Mastercard’s new Money in Motion report, compiled by Bain & Company. The findings point to a fast-changing market, as SMEs look for more efficient ways to move money across borders. 
 
The report, based on a survey of SMEs across 11 countries, suggests the market could look very different by 2028, as competition intensifies in a fast-growing sector. The overall B2B cross-border payments market is set to grow by 51%, from $31.7 trillion in 2024 to $47.8 trillion by 2032.2 Against that backdrop, smaller specialist providers are projected to become the leading choice for SMEs’ cross-border payment needs. By then, 48% are expected to choose a fintech as their main provider, up from 30% in 2025, while 28% are expected to select a bank, compared with 42% in 2025.
 
The research shows that SME priorities are changing. Trust (35%) and speed (34%) are now the biggest considerations when selecting a cross-border payment provider, with cost and transparency close behind at 28% each. Among SMEs that have recently changed providers, two in three (67%) say faster transactions and more reliable settlements were the driving force. Once selected, trust remains the strongest anchor for loyalty in an increasingly fluid market.
 
More than nine in 10 (92%) SMEs surveyed already use multiple payment providers, showing that many are spreading their business across different partners to meet their cross-border payment needs.
 

“SMEs are rethinking what they need from cross-border payments. They are using more providers, comparing options more closely and becoming more willing to switch. For banks and fintechs, that creates a clear opportunity to win and keep their business by delivering the speed, trust and transparency SMEs now expect,” says Pratik Khowala, Global Head of Transfer Solutions, Mastercard.
 
SMEs are also looking beyond the payment itself. The report shows that they want more visibility, control andtools that help them manage risk and reconcile payments more easily. Payment tracking (43%) and fraud detection (42%) are the two most sought-after value-added services, showing how important the wider payment experience has become. 
 

Pratik Khowala continues: “Banks and fintechs cannot afford to treat cross-border payments as a back-office service. For SMEs, it is becoming a test of whether a provider understands their business. Those that keep pace can build deeper relationships. Those that do not risk losing not just payment volumes, but the wider SME relationship.”
 
How SME money movement priorities vary across markets
In Indonesia and India, SMEs are among the most likely to shop around, with 34% and 29%, respectively,using at least four providers, compared with an average of 19% across the countries surveyed. 
In the UK, transparency is critical for building loyalty, with 45% saying clear pricing makes them more likely to choose or stay with a provider, compared with 38% globally.
In the US, 44% say real-time updates on payment status would increase their loyalty to a provider or make them more likely to use more of its services, compared with 32% globally.
SMEs in Brazil are the most proactive in enhancing their cross-border payments, with six in 10 (60%) exploring additional tools, compared with a global average of 48%.
 



Joe Lischwe, Financial Services Partner at Bain & Company, comments: “As SMEs expand internationally, they are building more relationships with customers, suppliers and partners across borders, and that is changing what they need from payment providers. Trust remains the anchor, but the fundamentals of the payment experience like reliability, transparency and efficiency increasingly need to simply work. The winners will be those that combine that trusted foundation with greater visibility, control and flexibility as their customers’ needs evolve.”
 
Racing all over the world
Mastercard has teamed up with the McLaren Mastercard Formula 1® Team and world champion Lando Norris to bring the world of racing and cross-border payments together. The McLaren Mastercard Formula 1® Team races across more than 20 cities during a racing season and works with hundreds of suppliers around the world, making fast, efficient global money movement a vital part of its operations.
 
The collaboration has resulted in a new film showing Mastercard’s technology in action, with an end-to-end cross-continental payment going head-to-head with the McLaren Mastercard Formula 1® Team’s fastest-ever pit stop of 1.8 seconds, set in 2023. Mastercard recorded a similar milestone in March, when a payment from the US to the Philippines took just under one second.
 

Laura Bowden, Chief Financial Officer, McLaren Racing, comments: “Every fraction of a second matters to us on track, and that same discipline extends to how we run the business behind the scenes. We work with partners and suppliers across the world, so payments need to move quickly, reliably and with as little friction as possible.” 
 
McLaren uses Airwallex to support its cross-border payment needs. Airwallex, in turn, connects to Mastercard Move, leveraging its global payout network to help facilitate fast, reliable and transparent payments for its customers. 
 
Mastercard Move enables banks, fintechs and other payment providers – and their customers – to send and receive funds quickly, securely and transparently. Built on Mastercard’s trusted card and non-card networks, it supports domestic and international transfers across more than 200 countries and territories and in over 150 currencies, connecting to bank accounts, digital wallets, cards and cash endpoints.

content: A new Mastercard and Bain & Company report reveals that 91 percent of internationally trading SMEs plan to switch cross-border payment providers within two years. Driven by demands for speed, trust, and transparency, smaller fintech providers are expected to surpass traditional banks. The report highlights shifting SME priorities, increased use of multiple providers, and the demand for advanced tools like fraud detection and payment tracking.

title: Stablecoin cross-border flows surge 78%, defying crypto bear market
summary: Cross-border stablecoin transfers surged as the wider crypto market shrank 37%, with Chainalysis pointing to growing use for trade, remittances and savings.
content: Cross-border stablecoin transfers surged by 78 percent even as the wider cryptocurrency market contracted by 37 percent. According to Chainalysis, this growth highlights the increasing adoption of stablecoins for international trade, remittances, and savings, demonstrating resilience despite challenging market conditions.

title: Bybit Adds PATH, CYPH And HUT Equity Perpetuals With Up To 25x Leverage
summary: TL;DR Bybit has added USDT-margined perpetual futures tied to PATH, CYPH and HUT shares. The contracts offer up to 25x leverage through Bybit’s TradFi perpetual desk. These are synthetic derivatives tracking equity prices, not spot shares or direct stock ownership. Bybit is continuing to turn its crypto derivatives platform into a 24/7 market for traditional assets. The exchange has added new USDT-margined perpetual contracts tied to UiPath, Cypherpunk Technologies and Hut 8, using the equity tickers PATH, CYPH and HUT. Equity Prices, Crypto-Style Trading The contracts sit inside Bybit’s TradFi perpetuals product and can offer leverage of up to 25x. For users, that means the trading mechanics look much closer to crypto perpetuals than to a conventional brokerage account. Positions are margined and settled through the exchange’s derivatives infrastructure, while the contracts track the referenced equity prices through index and oracle feeds. That makes the products accessible around the clock, but it also creates a very different risk profile from simply owning the underlying shares. There are no voting rights or physical stock delivery attached to the perpetual positions. Crypto Venues Are Becoming Multi-Asset Derivatives Platforms Hut 8 gives the launch an obvious crypto connection, while UiPath and Cypherpunk Technologies broaden the range further. The more interesting shift is structural. Bybit, Binance and other large exchanges are increasingly using perpetual futures as a universal wrapper for prices that originate outside crypto. That can pull traditional-market speculation into an environment where leverage and continuous trading are already normal. For users, the convenience is clear. So is the need to keep the instrument straight: these are synthetic equity derivatives, not tokenized shares and not spot stock trades. This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
content: Bybit has introduced USDT-margined perpetual futures contracts tied to PATH, CYPH, and HUT equity prices, offering up to 25x leverage. title: Binance Brings 24/7 FX Perpetuals To Crypto Traders With USD/BRL
summary: TL;DR Binance Futures has launched a 24/7 perpetual contract tied to the USD/BRL foreign-exchange rate. USD/BRL is the first pair in the new FX-perpetual product line. The product gives synthetic leveraged FX exposure through a crypto derivatives venue; it is not spot foreign-exchange settlement. Binance is moving another traditional market into the always-on crypto trading model. The exchange has launched 24/7 foreign-exchange perpetuals, beginning with a contract tied to the US dollar and Brazilian real. USD/BRL Is The First Pair The initial contract gives traders continuous synthetic exposure to the USD/BRL exchange rate using the perpetual-futures format already familiar across crypto markets. That removes the conventional weekend and overnight boundaries associated with many FX venues. For crypto-native traders, the product also means foreign-exchange exposure can sit alongside Bitcoin, Ethereum and other derivatives inside the same collateral and risk-management environment. The launch pair is USD/BRL. Binance has indicated that additional FX contracts are expected, but the September 21 rollout should not be read as the simultaneous launch of every major currency pair. Crypto Exchanges Keep Expanding Into TradFi Markets The broader trend is becoming difficult to miss. Major crypto derivatives venues are no longer limiting themselves to crypto assets. Equity-linked perpetuals, pre-IPO contracts and now foreign-exchange products are increasingly being offered through the same 24/7 infrastructure. That creates a different trading experience from the underlying markets. A perpetual contract provides price exposure, but it does not mean the trader is receiving or delivering physical currency. The USD/BRL launch is therefore less about Binance becoming a conventional FX bank and more about crypto-style derivatives becoming a wrapper for a wider range of financial prices. This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

content_ta: FBI தனது வருடாந்திர Virtual Asset Technical Exchange மாநாட்டை சமீபத்தில் நடத்தியது. இந்த மாநாட்டில் சட்ட அமலாக்க அதிகாரிகளும், புலனாய்வாளர்களும், crypto-security நிபுணர்களும் கலந்துகொண்டனர். டிஜிட்டல் சொத்துக்கள் தொடர்பான பல்வேறு குற்றச் செயல்கள் குறித்த தகவல்களைப் பகிர்ந்து கொள்ளவும், ஒத்துழைப்புடன் செயல்படவும் இந்த சந்திப்பு ஒரு தளமாக அமைகிறது.

title: Crypto Long & Short: Inside the chain settling $150 billion of stablecoins a week
summary: Tron launched as a content-distribution project and has become the settlement layer for a large share of the world's USDT, processing roughly $150 billion to $190 billion of stablecoin transfers a week. Josh Olszewicz of Canary Capital breaks down how the network's economics work and what stablecoin regulation could do to the thesis.
content: Tron has evolved from a content-distribution project into a major settlement layer for stablecoins, processing roughly $150 billion to $190 billion in USDT transfers weekly. Josh Olszewicz of Canary Capital recently examined the network's underlying economics and discussed the potential impact that future stablecoin regulations might have on its ongoing growth and thesis.
content_ta: Tron ஒரு கன்டென்ட்-டிஸ்ட்ரிபியூஷன் திட்டமாகத் தொடங்கி, தற்போது ஸ்டேபிள்காயின்களுக்கான முக்கிய செட்டில்மென்ட் லேயராக வளர்ந்துள்ளது. இது வாரத்திற்கு தோராயமாக $150 பில்லியன் முதல் $190 பில்லியன் வரை USDT பரிமாற்றங்களைக் கையாளுகிறது. Canary Capital-ஐச் சேர்ந்த Josh Olszewicz, இந்த நெட்வொர்க்கின் பொருளாதார நிலை மற்றும் எதிர்கால ஸ்டேபிள்காயின் ஒழுங்குமுறைகள் இதன் வளர்ச்சியில் என்ன தாக்கத்தை ஏற்படுத்தும் என்பதை ஆராய்ந்துள்ளார்.

title: Bitwise launches first Lighter ETP amid Hyperliquid rivalry

content: Bitwise has launched the first Lighter ETP in Europe, expanding its offerings tied to decentralized derivatives platforms. The new product provides European investors with brokerage access to the LIT token. content_ta: Bitwise நிறுவனம் ஐரோப்பாவில் முதல் Lighter ETP-ஐ அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. இந்த புதிய தயாரிப்பு ஐரோப்பிய முதலீட்டாளர்களுக்கு LIT டோக்கனை தரகர் மூலம் அணுகும் வசதியை வழங்குகிறது. பரவலாக்கப்பட்ட டெரிவேட்டிவ்கள் துறையில் Hyperliquid நிறுவனத்துடனான போட்டியின் மத்தியில் இந்த நடவடிக்கை எடுக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: Americans Would Use Stablecoins—If They Came With Bank Protections, Visa Study Finds
summary: A Visa survey found U.S. willingness to use stablecoins for cross-border transfers rises from 36% to 56% when paired with hypothetical bank-level fraud protection and deposit insurance.
content: A recent Visa study reveals that U.S. consumer willingness to use stablecoins for cross-border money transfers increases significantly when backed by traditional financial safeguards. According to the survey, adoption interest jumps from 36 percent to 56 percent if these digital assets include hypothetical bank-level fraud protection and deposit insurance, highlighting the importance of consumer trust in digital currency adoption.
content_ta: Visa நடத்திய சமீபத்திய ஆய்வின்படி, பாரம்பரிய வங்கி பாதுகாப்பு அம்சங்கள் வழங்கப்பட்டால், அமெரிக்காவில் உள்ள மக்கள் cross-border பணப் பரிமாற்றங்களுக்கு stablecoins பயன்படுத்தும் ஆர்வம் கணிசமாக அதிகரிக்கிறது. இத்தகைய டிஜிட்டல் சொட்டுகளில் வங்கி அளவிலான மோசடி பாதுகாப்பு மற்றும் வைப்பு காப்பீடு வழங்கப்பட்டால், பயன்படுத்துவதற்கான விருப்பம் 36 சதவீதத்திலிருந்து 56 சதவீதமாக உயரும் என்று அந்த ஆய்வு காட்டுகிறது.

title: Bitcoin Dips, But Its Forks Are Flying Again
summary: A CME futures listing and a fresh Grayscale ETF filing sent Bitcoin's two biggest forks soaring, even as the flagship coin cooled off its seven-month high.
content: Bitcoin experienced a slight cooldown from its seven-month high, but its two largest fork cryptocurrencies surged significantly. This upward momentum in the fork assets was driven by a new CME futures listing and a fresh exchange-traded fund filing by Grayscale, capturing renewed investor interest while the flagship cryptocurrency temporarily lost some steam.
content_ta: ஏழு மாத உச்சத்தில் இருந்த Bitcoin விலை சற்று குறைந்தாலும், அதன் இரண்டு முக்கிய forks சொத்துக்களின் மதிப்பு கணிசமாக உயர்ந்தது. CME futures பட்டியல் மற்றும் Grayscale-இன் புதிய ETF தாக்கல் ஆகியவை இந்த fork சொத்துக்களின் உயர்வுக்கு காரணமாக அமைந்தன, இதன் மூலம் முதன்மை கிரிப்டோகரன்சி சற்று மந்தமடைந்த நிலையிலும் முதலீட்டாளர்களின் கவனம் மீண்டும் ஈர்க்கப்பட்டது.

title: ‘BTC still has room to catch up’: Bitcoin’s $80,000 breakout draws institutional demand as analysts weigh durability
summary: K33, Nexo and 21shares weigh in on bitcoin's breakout as ETF inflows hit their highest since Nov. 2024. Key levels: $87K–88K resistance.
content: Bitcoin recently broke out past the $80,000 level, drawing strong institutional demand as exchange-traded fund inflows reached their highest levels since November 2024. Industry analysts from firms like K33, Nexo, and 21Shares are currently evaluating the durability of this upward momentum, highlighting key resistance levels between $87,000 and $88,000 as the cryptocurrency continues to show significant market strength.
content_ta: Bitcoin சமீப, $80,000 விலையைத் தாண்டி சாதனை படைத்துள்ளது. இதனால் ETF முதலீடுகள் நவம்பர் 2024-க்குப் பிறகு மிக உயர்ந்த அளவை எட்டியுள்ளன, மேலும் நிறுவனங்களின் தேவையும் அதிகரித்துள்ளது. K33, Nexo மற்றும் 21shares போன்ற நிறுவனங்களின் ஆய்வாளர்கள் இந்த விலை உயர்வின் நிலையகத்தன்மையை ஆராய்ந்து வருகின்றனர். $87,000 முதல் $88,000 வரையிலான முக்கிய எதிர்ப்பு நிலைகளை அவர்கள் கண்காணித்து வருகின்றனர்.

title: Stablecoins hold nearly $200 billion in US debt, but money funds bought the surge
summary:
Treasury says money-market mutual funds absorbed about 85% of more than $550 billion in new bill supply during July and August.

content: Recent U.S. Treasury data reveals that stablecoins now hold nearly $200 billion in US debt. However, money-market mutual funds primarily drove the recent surge, absorbing about 85% of more than $550 billion in new Treasury bill supply issued over the summer months.
content_ta: புதிய U.S. Treasury தரவுகளின்படி, Stablecoins தற்போது கிட்டத்தட்ட $200 பில்லியன் மதிப்பிலான US கடனை வைத்துள்ளன. இருப்பினும், இந்த அதிகரிப்புக்கு முக்கிய காரணம் money-market mutual funds ஆகும், இவை கோடை மாதங்களில் வெளியிடப்பட்ட $550 பில்லியனுக்கும் அதிகமான புதிய Treasury bill சப்ளையில் சுமார் 85% ஐ உறிஞ்சின.

title: Bitcoin ETFs just erased a $5.7 billion hole, but profit-taking is swallowing the new demand
summary:
A second large inflow met weak price follow-through. Dated fund reports and an earlier rise in profit taking leave the seller behind the move unidentified.
The post Bitcoin ETFs just erased a $5.7 billion hole, but profit-taking is swallowing the new demand appeared first on CryptoSlate.
content: Bitcoin ETFs have successfully recovered billions in losses, balancing out previous market declines. However, ongoing profit-taking activities are quickly absorbing the surge in new demand. Despite significant inflows into these funds, the lack of strong price follow-through leaves the identity of the primary sellers uncertain as the market navigates these shifting dynamics.
content_ta: Bitcoin ETF-கள் பல பில்லியன் டாலர் இழப்புகளை வெற்றிகரமாக மீட்டுள்ளன, முந்தைய சந்தை சரிவுகளை ஈடுகட்டுகின்றன. இருப்பினும், தொடர்ந்து லாபம் பெறும் நடவடிக்கைகள் புதிய தேவையின் உயர்வை விரைவாக ஈர்த்து வருகின்றன. இந்த நிதிகளில் குறிப்பிடத்தக்க முதலீடுகள் வந்தாலும், வலுவான விலை உயர்வு இல்லாததால், இந்த சந்தை மாற்றங்களுக்கு மத்தியில் முக்கிய விற்பனையாளர்கள் யார் என்பது தெளிவாகத் தெரியவில்லை.

content_ta: Sebastián Marset, Uruguay-ஐச் சேர்ந்த கொக்கைன்-மாஃபியா மற்றும் crypto kingpin என்று வர்ணிக்கப்படுகிறார். முறையான crypto குற்ற அமைப்பு எதுவும் நிரூபிக்கப்படாவிட்டாலும், digital currency மூலம் பணம் சலவை செய்யப்பட்டதற்கான ஆதாரங்கள் குற்றவியல் நடவடிக்கைகளின் தடங்களை கண்டறிய உதவுவதை Marset வழக்கு காட்டுகிறது.

title: Bybit Adds Support For Avalanche v1.15.0 Network Upgrade
summary: TL;DR Bybit has confirmed support for Avalanche’s v1.15.0 network upgrade. The exchange is updating its Avalanche node infrastructure while keeping AVAX trading active. The announcement concerns network compatibility and exchange operations, not a change to AVAX supply or token economics. Bybit has confirmed that its Avalanche infrastructure will support the network’s v1.15.0 upgrade, giving AVAX users one less exchange-compatibility issue to worry about during the transition. The September 22 notice covers both AVAX and Avalanche C-Chain support. Exchange Nodes Need To Move With The Network When a blockchain ships a network upgrade, exchanges have to update the software that connects deposits, withdrawals and internal wallet systems to the chain. If they do not, customer transfers can stall even while spot trading remains available. Bybit says it is updating its validator and node infrastructure for the Avalanche v1.15.0 release while maintaining trading during the synchronization process. That makes this primarily an infrastructure story. Users are not being asked to migrate tokens, claim a new asset or swap AVAX into a different contract. The Upgrade Does Not Change AVAX Tokenomics The Bybit notice is also useful for what it does not say. There is no token redenomination, supply-cap change or new asset created as part of the exchange support process. The work is about keeping Bybit’s backend aligned with the upgraded Avalanche network. For users, that should translate into continued exchange support once node synchronization is complete. For Avalanche, exchange adoption of a network release is one of the quieter but necessary steps in moving new software into production at scale. This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
content: Bybit has announced its support for the Avalanche v1.15.0 network upgrade. The exchange is currently updating its node and validator infrastructure to ensure smooth operations. AVAX spot trading will remain active during this synchronization process, and users are not required to swap tokens or perform any migration. This routine technical update focuses entirely on backend network compatibility rather than any changes to AVAX tokenomics.
content_ta: Avalanche-யின் v1.15.0 நெட்வொர்க் மேம்படுத்தலுக்கான ஆதரவை Bybit உறுதிப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. பரிமாற்றம் தனது நோட் மற்றும் வேலிடேட்டர் உள்கட்டமைப்பை தடையற்ற செயல்பாடுகளுக்காக புதுப்பித்து வருகிறது. இந்த ஒத்திசைவு செயல்பாட்டின் போது AVAX ஸ்பாட் வர்த்தகம் வழக்கம்போல செயல்படும். பயனர்கள் டோக்கன்களை மாற்றவோ அல்லது வேறு எதையும் செய்யவோ தேவையில்லை. இந்தத் தொழில்நுட்ப மேம்பாடு பின்னணி நெட்வொர்க் இணக்கத்தன்மையை மட்டுமே சார்ந்துள்ளது.

title: Bybit Opens Oura Pre-IPO Perpetual Trading With Up To 25x Leverage
summary: TL;DR Bybit has added USDT-margined perpetual futures tied to PATH, CYPH and HUT shares. The contracts offer up to 25x leverage through Bybit’s TradFi perpetual desk. These are synthetic derivatives tracking equity prices, not spot shares or direct stock ownership. Bybit is continuing to turn its crypto derivatives platform into a 24/7 market for traditional assets. The exchange has added new USDT-margined perpetual contracts tied to UiPath, Cypherpunk Technologies and Hut 8, using the equity tickers PATH, CYPH and HUT. Equity Prices, Crypto-Style Trading The contracts sit inside Bybit’s TradFi perpetuals product and can offer leverage of up to 25x. For users, that means the trading mechanics look much closer to crypto perpetuals than to a conventional brokerage account. Positions are margined and settled through the exchange’s derivatives infrastructure, while the contracts track the referenced equity prices through index and oracle feeds. That makes the products accessible around the clock, but it also creates a very different risk profile from simply owning the underlying shares. There are no voting rights or physical stock delivery attached to the perpetual positions. Crypto Venues Are Becoming Multi-Asset Derivatives Platforms Hut 8 gives the launch an obvious crypto connection, while UiPath and Cypherpunk Technologies broaden the range further. The more interesting shift is structural. Bybit, Binance and other large exchanges are increasingly using perpetual futures as a universal wrapper for prices that originate outside crypto. That can pull traditional-market speculation into an environment where leverage and continuous trading are already normal. For users, the convenience is clear. So is the need to keep the instrument straight: these are synthetic equity derivatives, not tokenized shares and not spot stock trades. This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Binance Lets bStocks Tokenized Equities Count As Futures Margin
summary: TL;DR Binance now allows eligible bStocks tokenized-equity holdings to be used as collateral in Multi-Assets Mode. The feature lets users retain exposure to tokenized stocks while using their collateral value for futures positions. Regional restrictions and risk haircuts still apply. Binance is giving its tokenized-stock product a second job. Eligible bStocks holdings can now be used as collateral inside the exchange‘s Multi-Assets Mode, allowing users to keep tokenized equity exposure while putting part of that value to work against futures margin requirements. Tokenized Stocks Move Into The Collateral Layer Until now, tokenized equities were largely a trading product. Using them as collateral changes the role they can play inside an exchange account. A user holding an eligible bStock can keep the position while the exchange recognizes a haircut-adjusted portion of its value for margin purposes. That does not remove risk. Collateral haircuts can change with volatility and account settings, and losses in a leveraged futures position can still put the collateral at risk. But it makes bStocks more integrated with the rest of Binance’s derivatives infrastructure. Tokenization Gets More Useful When Assets Become Composable One of the recurring arguments for tokenized securities is that they can do more than simply mimic the price of a conventional asset. Collateral use is a concrete example. Once a tokenized equity can be moved, pledged or used inside another financial product, it starts behaving more like a native digital asset than a static wrapper. Binance’s rollout remains subject to regional eligibility and KYC restrictions, so “available to all users” should not be interpreted as universal availability in every jurisdiction. Within eligible accounts, however, bStocks have now moved beyond trading into margin utility. This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
content: Binance now allows eligible bStocks tokenized-equity holdings to be used as collateral in its Multi-Assets Mode. This update enables users to retain exposure to tokenized stocks while utilizing their collateral value for futures positions, subject to regional restrictions and risk haircuts.
content_ta: Binance-ல் தகுதியான bStocks டோக்கனைஸ் செய்யப்பட்ட ஈக்விட்டி பங்குகளை Multi-Assets Mode-க்கான பிணையமாகப் (collateral) பயன்படுத்த அனுமதிக்கப்படுகிறது. இந்த புதிய அம்சத்தின் மூலம் பயனர்கள் தங்கள் டோக்கனைஸ் செய்யப்பட்ட பங்குகளின் மீதான முதலீட்டைத் தக்கவைத்துக்கொண்டு, ஃபியூச்சர்ஸ் பொசிஷன்களுக்கு அந்தப் பிணைய மதிப்பைப் பயன்படுத்திக் கொள்ள முடியும்.

content: A recent report by Nexo reveals that 67 percent of affluent investors currently own crypto, yet only a few integrate it into their core wealth plans. Meanwhile, investors in the United States demonstrate the deepest crypto integration despite recording lower overall ownership rates compared to other regions.

title: Five Reasons Why UPI Has Not Disrupted Credit Card
summary: Author: A finextra community member
content: Despite the massive growth of UPI in digital payments, several factors explain why it has not fully disrupted the credit card market. UPI primarily serves instant bank-to-bank transfers and debit-like transactions, whereas credit cards offer distinct advantages such as deferred payments, credit building, reward programs, and built-in fraud protection. title: Boaz Lahovitsky Joins Broadridge as President of Wealth Management
summary:
Broadridge today announced that Boaz Lahovitsky has joined the company as President of Wealth Management. Lahovitsky succeeds Mike Alexander, who will remain with the company working on strategic programs and initiatives.
 

“Boaz is an accomplished operating leader with a powerful track record of building and scaling wealth management businesses, advancing digital innovation, and delivering profitable growth,” said Tom Carey, Broadridge’s Global Head of Product and Technology. “His experience across advice, technology, data, and client engagement makes him exceptionally well positioned to lead our Wealth Management business into its next chapter. Mike is a highly respected leader, and I look forward to partnering with him on the initiatives ahead. He has built an exceptional franchise and will work closely with Boaz to ensure a seamless leadership transition and advance our growth strategy for Wealth Management.”
 
Lahovitsky brings over 20 years of experience building and scaling advisory and platform businesses at leading financial institutions. Most recently, he served as Managing Director of Personal Advisors at J.P. Morgan, where he built the bank’s hybrid-advice business for mass-affluent clients by bringing together fiduciary investment advice, advisor platforms, and digital client engagement. His background also includes senior roles at Vanguard, Citi, Genpact, UBS, and Booz Allen Hamilton. At Vanguard, Lahovitsky led the company’s high-net-worth Advisors driving significant growth in assets under management. At Genpact and Citi, he led wealth management platform and BPO businesses, after holding strategy, transformation, and M&A roles earlier in his career.
 

“Broadridge has an exceptional reputation for helping the wealth management industry innovate, operate, and grow more effectively while creating better outcomes for investors,” said Lahovitsky. “I am excited to join this talented team and build on the strong foundation Mike and the Wealth leadership organization have established. Together, we have an opportunity to further strengthen our platform, help our clients navigate a rapidly changing market, and drive the next generation of growth in a time of great inflection in our industry through advancements in Artificial Intelligence and Digital Assets.”
 
Broadridge is shaping the next generation of wealth management by empowering wealth management firms to better navigate a constantly changing industry. The Broadridge Wealth Platform, an open-architected ecosystem of solutions, helps clients modernize their tech stacks to drive business growth, increase advisor productivity, improve investor experiences, and digitize and modernize the governance, communications, and operational foundation that support growth and long-term value creation. With over 50 years of partnering with thousands of clients to reinvent wealth technologies, Broadridge has the proven track record to help clients push the boundaries of what’s next.

title: NG.CASH Raises $15 Million to Expand Credit and Financial Access for Brazil's Next Generation
summary:
NG.CASH, a Brazilian fintech rooted in the creator economy and built for a new generation's relationship with money, today announced a $15 million strategic investment led by Blockchain Capital, bringing the company's total funding raised since its 2021 founding to over $65 million.
NG.CASH, in 2021, started as an offshoot of a YouTube channel with 10 million subscribers, which has since grown to 20 million, and has grown into a platform serving more than 10 million users. The round comes as leading venture firms increasingly look to de-risk from an oversaturated U.S. market by backing category-defining companies in large international markets like Brazil.
"Millions of young Brazilians have grown up without a financial platform built for the way they actually live and bank," said Mario Augusto Sá, NG.CASH's CEO and Co-founder. "Blockchain Capital's investment confirms NG.CASH is becoming that platform, the company building what comes next as money itself evolves in Brazil."
NG.CASH's core users come from middle- and lower-income households across Brazil, many from families where parents have never had a bank account of their own. For a lot of these users, NG.CASH is the first financial account anyone in the family has opened.
The company holds two Central Bank of Brazil licenses, a direct credit society license and a payment institution license. It has a Virtual Asset Service Provider (VASP) license application in process, giving it a regulatory foundation few can match. NG.CASH has grown to more than 10 million accounts since its 2021 founding, with billions of dollars already transacted on the platform. Credit products including Crédito CLT and Pix Crédito are driving that growth, and the company is targeting BRL 1 billion (nearly $200M USD) in credit originated by 2027.
"We've spent years looking outside the U.S. for the next generation of category-defining fintech companies," said Kinjal Shah, General Partner at Blockchain Capital. "Brazil is exactly the kind of market we believe will produce them. NG.CASH has already proven it can build and scale a business young Brazilians actually use, and that's why exactly why we wanted to invest."
NG.CASH's own history as a mass-market distributor, born from a YouTube channel and grown into a large financial platform, positions it to become one of the first movers on stablecoin and crypto adoption at scale in Brazil.

title: Almost Half of Brits Would Let Bots Shop for Them as AI-Driven Spending Is Set to Top £99bn Within Five Years
summary:
Nearly half of UK adults (48%) have already used, or would consider using, an AI agent to shop within the next 12 months, according to new research from Global Payments Inc. . This marks a significant increase from just 31% a year ago, signaling that shopping bots are rapidly gaining acceptance.
Brits are ready to let AI hunt for bargains
The findings suggest the traditional online buying journey could be on the verge of a major shake-up. More than two-thirds (69%) say they would consider using an AI agent if it could consistently find the best prices, reducing the need to spend hours searching, scrolling and comparing products.
If adoption takes off, AI agents could account for a projected £99 billion of UK retail spending annually by 2031. Within five years, Brits predict that AI bots will make around 16% of their purchases – more than double what they predicted last year (7%).
“For years, online shopping has meant opening dozens of tabs in search of the best deal. What's striking is how quickly consumers are becoming comfortable with letting AI do that work for them,” said Harsh Mehta, head of partnerships – AI and Agentic Commerce at Global Payments®. “The scale of spending that consumers expect AI to influence shows why businesses need to prepare for these new shopping journeys now.”
Retailers face a trust challenge
Despite growing enthusiasm, consumers draw the line when AI moves from recommending products to spending money. Shoppers are keen to benefit from automated searching and price comparison while retaining control over what is purchased and how much is spent.
Among consumers open to AI-powered purchasing:
90% would let an AI agent spend up to £100 on groceries and everyday essentials
84% would permit spending up to £100 on clothing and footwear
74% would allow spending up to £100 on luxury clothing and footwear
60% would cap spending on electronics and gadgets at £100
The findings reveal a trust gap. While consumers see clear value in AI-powered shopping, most are not yet comfortable giving bots significant access to their money. At least 95% would set a spending limit of £500 or less.[4]
Security remains the biggest barrier to adoption. More than half (54%) are concerned about the safety of their payment details, while nearly half (48%) worry about how their personal data could be used.
Consumers also want reassurance that they remain in control. More than a third (34%) want to confirm every purchase before a payment is made, 33% want access to human support when something goes wrong and 32% want evidence that the AI cannot be hacked or manipulated.
Harsh Mehta added, "Consumers are increasingly comfortable letting AI find the right product and the best price, but handing over the final purchasing decision is a much bigger leap. The opportunity is immense, but trust will determine how quickly AI shopping agents become standard practice. That's why we are focused on helping merchants deliver AI-powered shopping experiences that are secure, transparent and keep consumers in control."

title: Financial IT Fall Edition 2026
summary:
The Big Calls Edition   Welcome to an edition of Financial IT that is rather different to all others that we have published.    In many of the previous editions, it has been possible to link most of the articles to themes that feature prominently at major conferences where we have been a media partner. In some editions, almost all articles have related to a topic that is particularly current. With the help of our contributors, we have been able to share expert opinion in order to look at issues in great depth.   This edition is not linked to a particular conference or to a particular theme. However, a diverse variety of contributed articles lead to four major insights into the intersection of financial services and technology. This is the Big Calls Edition of Financial IT.   People don’t entirely trust AI yet - and that may be a good thing   At the time of writing of this Editor-in-Chief’s letter (mid-September 2026), the mainstream media (in the English-speaking world, at least) is pre-occupied with the possibility that Artificial Intelligence (AI) destroys humanity. Some commentators are calling for the development of AI systems to be slowed.   An important message from our contributors is that, for now, it is people who are in charge of AI - and  not the other way. As one of them observes: “AI will become an essential compliance tool— but it will not replace human judgment.” A key issue is trust - or the lack of it. As another contributor notes: “The research revealed that consumers are broadly comfortable using AI for search, discovery and price comparison. However, trust falls sharply at checkout. Agentic commerce will only expand beyond support for searching and price comparison if trust is built into the checkout journey from the start.”   A third contributor emphasises the need for transparency when AI is used to provide solutions: “The customer [does not have] to understand the AI model, but they do need to understand why a pricing, credit, or risk decision was made, and how it affects them, and who remains accountable for the outcome. Guardrails are what make innovation scalable, and AI must be as compliant as it is intelligent.”   Actual implementation of AI in financial services through 2027 may be slower than most people have been expecting.   Stablecoins could and should bring a revolution to cross-border payments   Customer experience in cross-border payments can and should improve further. According to one of our contributors: “businesses feel that gap directly: nearly one-third of cross-border payments still cost more than 3%, and only 40% of B2B transfers settle within a single working day. The network they lean on is thinning, too: the global supply of correspondent banking relationships has fallen 20% since the mid-2000s, and some corridors now have no intermediary at all.   Nevertheless, a solution is to hand - stablecoins. As one of contributors points out: “the demand for stablecoins is greater where they are easier to source than dollars through local exchanges: for example, in India, Nigeria, Brazil, Indonesia, Argentina. [Meanwhile], a large corporation in a developed market has no difficulty opening a dollar or euro account. Holding stablecoins isn’t going to solve a problem that that corporation doesn’t have. What it does need, however, is speed, transparency and lower transfer costs, without having digital assets on its balance sheet.”    This presents new opportunities for intermediaries. “When a payment starts in stablecoins, somebody in the middle has to take the asset, convert it to local currency, screen the counterparty and produce reconcilable records. Similarly, when a business pays local currency to freelancers or suppliers who would rather receive stablecoins, that intermediary provider is needed.”    Such an intermediary, moving stablecoins between wallets, will also need to build the trust of its customers. Expect this to be a developing story through 2027.   Wallets make multi-currency accounts more likely for all   Wallets are, of course, not just for stablecoins. Nor are they necessarily the favoured method of payment across all national markets. Nevertheless, as one of our contributors suggests: “Many global initiatives are pushing cross-border money movement toward a model that is easier to operate, reconcile and scale. The common goal is a more connected environment for domestic instant payment systems, where global businesses can collect, hold, convert and distribute funds with less friction, while still supporting the local experiences users and partners expect. In that context, wallets support platforms in meeting the new requirements of global cross-border finance.”   In many developing countries, people are used to thinking in terms of more than one currency - often the local one and a major one such as the US dollar or euro. It is possible that this happens to a greater extent in developed countries - and especially in the event of a financial crisis. In this eventuality, look for the popularity of multi-currency wallets to grow rapidly.   Digital strategy plays a central role in any emerging market’s prospects   The last word in this Editor’s letter goes to … Uzbekistan. Since 2023, the government has been transforming the economy as envisaged in its “Uzbekistan 2030” strategy. Simultaneously, the government has boosted investment and employment in digital- and fintech- related areas, mainly through the IT Park network which spans the entire country (and not just Tashkent).    In the 1980s and the 1990s, the key question for any emerging market revolved around the assumptions underpinning the  development of the particular country being discussed. Were the assumptions still valid?  In the mid-2020s, Uzbekistan shows how it is now other things that really matter the most: is the digital strategy really supporting sustainable development? The emerging markets phenomenon is even more exciting than it was 30 years ago.   Once again, we thank our contributors and supporters - and wish all a successful 2026 conference season.   Andrew Hutchings, Editor-in-Chief, Financial IT financial_it_fall_edition_2026_digital.pdf23 Sep, 2026Yeshttps://cutt.ly/2yvQ08nS
